messages.subject: Strictly Positive Satorra-Bentler Chi Square Test
parts:
Hello,

I'm attempting to compute the strictly positive Satorra-Bentler chi-square test to compare 2- and 3-factor models of executive function. The two models converge in lavaan, but when I attempt to run the test I get the following error message:

> lavTestLRT(m1, m0, method = 'satorra.bentler.2010')
Error in colSums(S) : 'x' must be an array of at least two dimensions

The code I am using in lavaan is below:

m0 = '
WM =~ NA*BSS3 + NA*FSS3 + NA*LTRS3 + NA*SPRS3 
AC =~ NA*SSUS3 + NA*SIMP3 + NA*TNT3 
IR =~ NA*STRP3 + NA*FLNK3 + NA*TKSW3 + NA*BOX3

# (Co)variances
WM ~~ a*IR
WM ~~ 1*AC
IR ~~ a*AC
WM ~~ 1*WM
AC ~~ 1*AC
IR ~~ 1*IR
BSS3 ~~ BSS3
FSS3 ~~ FSS3
LTRS3 ~~ LTRS3
SPRS3 ~~ SPRS3
SSUS3 ~~ SSUS3
SIMP3 ~~ SIMP3
TNT3 ~~ TNT3
FLNK3 ~~ FLNK3
STRP3 ~~ STRP3
TKSW3 ~~ TKSW3
BOX3 ~~ BOX3

# Intercepts
WM ~ 0*1
IR ~ 0*1
AC ~ 0*1
BSS3 ~ 1
FSS3 ~ 1
LTRS3 ~ 1
SPRS3 ~ 1
SSUS3 ~ 1
SIMP3 ~ 1
TNT3 ~ 1
FLNK3 ~ 1
STRP3 ~ 1
TKSW3 ~ 1
BOX3 ~ 1
'

m1 = '
WM =~ NA*BSS3 + NA*FSS3 + NA*LTRS3 + NA*SPRS3 
AC =~ NA*SSUS3 + NA*SIMP3 + NA*TNT3 
IR =~ NA*STRP3 + NA*FLNK3 + NA*TKSW3 + NA*BOX3

# (Co)variances
WM ~~ IR
WM ~~ AC
IR ~~ AC
WM ~~ 1*WM
AC ~~ 1*AC
IR ~~ 1*IR
BSS3 ~~ BSS3
FSS3 ~~ FSS3
LTRS3 ~~ LTRS3
SPRS3 ~~ SPRS3
SSUS3 ~~ SSUS3
SIMP3 ~~ SIMP3
TNT3 ~~ TNT3
FLNK3 ~~ FLNK3
STRP3 ~~ STRP3
TKSW3 ~~ TKSW3
BOX3 ~~ BOX3

# Intercepts
WM ~ 0*1
IR ~ 0*1
AC ~ 0*1
BSS3 ~ 1
FSS3 ~ 1
LTRS3 ~ 1
SPRS3 ~ 1
SSUS3 ~ 1
SIMP3 ~ 1
TNT3 ~ 1
FLNK3 ~ 1
STRP3 ~ 1
TKSW3 ~ 1
BOX3 ~ 1
'

m0 = cfa(m0, data = sub, estimator = 'MLR', missing = 'ML')
m1 = cfa(m1, data = sub, estimator = 'MLR', missing = 'ML')

summary(m0, standardized = T)
summary(m1, standardized = T)

lavTestLRT(m1, m0, method = 'satorra.bentler.2010')

I greatly appreciate any guidance on how I may resolve this issue.

Thank you,
Kristine

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Strictly Positive Satorra-Bentler Chi Square Test
parts: Error in colSums(S) : 'x' must be an array of at least two dimensions
Never seen this error before, but I wonder whether it would still occur if you didn't use the same object names for your syntax and model:

m0 = cfa(m0, data = sub, estimator = 'MLR', missing = 'ML')
m1 = cfa(m1, data = sub, estimator = 'MLR', missing = 'ML')

Because the strictly-positive method requires re-fitting one model holding parameters constant at estimates from the other model, I think it is trying to re-use the call stored within the lavaan object.  So try storing the result under a different name than the syntax object (which might need to be used in the call again).

fit0 <- cfa(m0, ...)
fit1 <- cfa(m1, ...)
